pageCache.text:
Opportunities for all
A Warm Welcome
Welcome to SENARP Vibe Independent School (SVIS) — a place where autistic children and young people feel understood, valued and able to succeed. Many of our pupils join us after finding education challenging elsewhere. At SVIS, we see this as the beginning of a new chapter, not a limitation.
Thank you for visiting our website and for trusting us to support your child’s journey. Please do get in touch if you would like to learn more about SENARP Vibe Independent School or arrange a visit — we would be delighted to welcome you.
Our Ethos
At SENARP Vibe Independent School (SVIS), we believe that every pupil should be supported to achieve their best possible outcomes. Our approach is centred on the development of our pupils, ensuring that academic learning, personal development and emotional wellbeing are given equal importance.
SVIS provides a safe, inclusive and nurturing environment in which pupils feel valued, listened to and supported to succeed. We work closely with families, professionals and the wider community to ensure that pupils are prepared not only for the next stage of education, but for life beyond school.
SVIS places a strong emphasis on the following:
Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education, safeguarding and Preparation for Adulthood, with a focus on relationships and personal safety.
Mental health and emotional wellbeing, including pupil voice, emotional literacy and self-regulation strategies.
Outdoor and experiential learning, promoting physical development, resilience and positive behaviour
Creative and expressive learning opportunities, including music, drama, art and movement, supporting communication, confidence and self-expression.
Learning Culture
At SENARP Vibe Independent School (SVIS), our curriculum is skills-focused and context-driven, promoting active engagement and purposeful learning. It is designed to support pupils in developing the key skills needed for both education and life beyond school, including communication, cognition, independence, physical development and self-care.

pageCache.pageTitle: SENARP Vibe Independent School - Headteacher Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headteacher Welcome
“Welcome to SENARP Vibe Independent School — a place where autistic children and young people feel understood, valued and able to succeed.Many of our pupils join us after finding education challenging elsewhere. At SENARP Vibe, we see this as the beginning of a new chapter, not a limitation.
Our school is built on strong relationships, clear structure and a belief that every child can thrive when the right support is in place. We provide calm, predictable environments where pupils feel safe, confident and ready to engage with learning — often experiencing success for the first time.
Preparing pupils for positive futures sits at the heart of everything we do. Alongside academic learning, we prioritise communication, emotional regulation, independence and life skills. Our highly personalised curriculum is shaped around each pupil’s strengths, interests and needs, supporting them to build confidence, resilience and self-belief.
We place great importance on positive, open and trusting relationships with parents and carers. We believe meaningful progress is achieved when school and home work together, with consistency in approaches playing a vital role in supporting pupils’ learning and wellbeing.
Our dedicated and skilled staff team bring expertise, creativity and genuine care to their work every day. They understand autism, value individuality and are committed to helping pupils overcome barriers and achieve their potential.
Thank you for visiting our website and for trusting us to support your child’s journey. Please do get in touch if you would like to learn more about SENARP Vibe Independent School or arrange a visit — we would be delighted to welcome you.”
Mrs Meryem Biridjik - Headteacher of SENARP Vibe Independent School

pageCache.pageTitle: SENARP Vibe Independent School - Home Partnership
pageCache.text:
Home Partnership
At SENARP Vibe Independent School (SVIS), we work in close partnership with parents, carers and families to support pupils to achieve their best possible outcomes. We recognise that strong, trusting relationships with families are central to pupil wellbeing, progress and success. Our approach is underpinned by clear systems and regular opportunities for communication and collaboration.
Open communication is a key priority at SVIS. Families are routinely shared information about their child’s learning, including personalised learning targets, timetables, curriculum aims and class updates. We promote a positive, solution-focused approach to communication that values collaboration, celebrates progress and supports problem-solving. Daily contact between home and school helps ensure consistency and shared understanding.
SVIS also uses an online evidence-based learning platform to share pupils’ achievements and progress with families on a regular basis. Families have secure access to view updates and are encouraged to contribute observations from home, helping staff build a fuller picture of each pupil and inform future planning. In addition, we welcome families into school throughout the year for shared learning experiences and celebrations, providing opportunities to engage with staff and peers in a supportive environment.
To further strengthen our community, SVIS hosts regular opportunities for parents and carers to connect, share ideas and access information. These sessions support relationship-building, promote parental engagement and provide opportunities to meet key members of the school team and external services. Through these partnerships, we aim to ensure families feel informed, valued and actively involved in their child’s education.

pageCache.pageTitle: SENARP Vibe Independent School - Our Learning Culture
pageCache.text:
Our Learning Culture
Tailored Curriculum
At SENARP Vibe Independent School (SVIS), our curriculum is skills-focused and context-driven, promoting active engagement and purposeful learning. It is designed to sup44port pupils in developing the key skills needed for both education and life beyond school, including communication, cognition, independence, physical development and self-care. These transferable skills underpin our approach and prepare pupils for future learning, employment and adulthood.
Our curriculum is responsive and personalised, recognising that every learner brings individual strengths, needs and interests. Learning is carefully planned to build on what pupils already know and can do, while offering appropriate challenge and progression.
A structured rolling programme is in place to ensure a balanced and coherent curriculum over time. This provides pupils with a range of meaningful learning experiences, delivered through varied themes, subjects and real-life contexts. Through this approach, pupils are supported to remain engaged, motivated and confident learners, while developing the knowledge, skills and independence needed to thrive.
Planning and Reflection
At SVIS, planning and reflective inquiry sit at the heart of our approach to teaching and learning. Staff work collaboratively to design learning that is purposeful, responsive and rooted in evidence. Our curriculum pathways provide clear intent and direction, while ongoing formative assessment and shared reflection ensure that teaching continually adapts to meet pupils’ needs. Evidence of learning is used thoughtfully to inform planning, ensuring that learning builds progressively and remains meaningful for every pupil.Reflective inquiry at SVIS is embedded within everyday practice and professional culture. Staff regularly reflect on pupil engagement, progress and wellbeing, using these insights to refine teaching strategies and shape future learning experiences. This continuous cycle of reflection, collaboration and review supports high-quality teaching, consistent practice across the school and strong outcomes for all learners.
Assessment and Progress
At SVIS, assessment is an ongoing and reflective process that places the pupil at the centre of decision-making. Evidence of learning is gathered regularly and used to understand progress, inform next steps and evaluate the impact of teaching. Assessment is closely linked to curriculum intent and personal learning goals, ensuring that learning remains aspirational, meaningful and appropriate to each pupil’s needs. This reflective approach supports consistent moderation, professional dialogue and continuous school improvement.
Assessment at SVIS is inclusive, flexible and responsive, recognising that pupils access learning through different pathways and develop at different rates. A range of assessment approaches are used to capture progress over time, support personalised learning intentions and strengthen communication with families. By combining professional judgement, evidence of learning and regular review, assessment at SVIS supports high expectations, celebrates progress and ensures that teaching and provision remain well matched to every learner.
Staffing Ratio
A key pillar of our educational model is the maintenance of a high staff-to-pupil ratio, which will ensure that each pupil receives the personalised attention and support necessary for their development. The staff body will include fully qualified teachers, teaching assistants, therapists, and other specialist professionals, selected for their demonstrable expertise and commitment to supporting children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities.
All staff members will undertake robust, ongoing training, tailored to meet the specific needs of our pupil cohort. This will include, but not be limited to, advanced communication strategies, positive behaviour support, safeguarding, and specialist methodologies such as SCERTS, TEACCH, Makaton, and sensory integration. We are confident that prioritising continuous professional development will result in positive educational and wellbeing outcomes for all pupils.

Key Term Dates and School Hours
At SENARP Vibe Independent School, we understand that predictability and consistency are essential for our pupils. Clear, reliable routines help our pupils feel safe, confident and ready to learn. pageCache.text:
Referall Process
Who Can Make a Referral
Referrals and enquiries can be made by:
For initial enquiries, please email us at contact@senarp.com
We aim to respond to all initial enquiries within 2-5 working days. The time taken to progress from initial enquiry to placement depends on the complexity of the case, the availability of documentation and the Local Authority's own processes, but we are committed to being as prompt and responsive as possible.
Our Referral Process
1. Initial Enquiry Contact us by phone or email to share a brief outline of the child or young person. At this stage, we can let you know whether we have current or anticipated capacity, and whether our provision is likely to be a good match.
2. Sharing of Information Where we feel there may be a match, we will ask for the following documents to be shared securely:
3. Assessment of Suitability Our leadership team will review the information provided and assess whether we are able to meet the pupil's needs safely and effectively. This includes considering the profile of the existing pupil cohort and the specialist skills of our staff team.
4. Placement Decision and Transition Planning If all parties agree SENARP Vibe is the right school, we work closely with the Local Authority, family and current setting to plan a smooth, phased transition tailored to the pupil's needs.

pageCache.pageTitle: SENARP Vibe Independent School - Senior Leadership Team
pageCache.text:
Senior Leadership Team
Rehana Talaimojeh – Founder, SENARP
Rehana has spent the last 13 years focusing on the development of SEND education. Rehana founded SENARP, focused on a holistic, 24-hour curriculum supporting both parents and children. This includes the pioneering Phoenix Home Project, as well as setting up multiple Additional Resource Provisions (ARPs) to train staff and create inclusive strategies to maximise the potential of autistic children with additional complex needs.
“Our mission is clear: to create learning environments that are truly child-centred, ensuring that every student, regardless of their challenges, has the opportunity to thrive.”
Dr. Alison Livemore - Consultant, SENARP
Alison is a doctoral researcher (PhD (c)) in autism education with over ten years leading teaching and learning for autistic pupils. Alison expertly guides teams to implement evidence-based, nurturing systems. She delivers comprehensive autism training for various stakeholders and has significant experience in curriculum management, including developing specialized curricula for pre-formal and semi-formal learners.
“Leading the teaching and learning of autistic pupils is a profoundly meaningful endeavour. It’s about recognising the unique strengths and needs of each child and fostering a love of learning that empowers them to succeed.”

pageCache.pageTitle: SENARP Vibe Independent School - Home Learning
pageCache.text:
Home Learning
At SENARP Vibe Independent School (SVIS), we recognise that learning does not stop at the end of the school day. Home learning plays an important role in reinforcing skills, promoting independence and supporting consistency between school and home. Where appropriate, pupils are provided with personalised home learning activities that reflect their individual needs, abilities and learning priorities. These activities are designed to be meaningful, achievable and supportive, rather than task-focused, and may include communication practice, life skills, sensory activities or preparation for adulthood goals.
We also understand that families benefit from practical guidance and structured support to help embed learning and therapeutic strategies at home. As part of the wider SENARP family, pupils and families at SVIS can request for our trailblazing SENARP Home Support (SHS), a specialist service that works alongside families to strengthen consistency, confidence and outcomes beyond the school environment. SENARP Home Support complements school provision by helping families implement strategies in everyday routines, supporting generalisation of skills and promoting positive engagement at home and within the community. This joined-up approach helps ensure that pupils experience continuity, stability and high-quality support across all aspects of their lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: SENARP Vibe Independent School - SALT Provisions
pageCache.text:
SALT Provisions
At SENARP Vibe Independent School (SVIS), our team of specialist Speech and Language Therapists (SaLT) work with all pupils to support the development of effective communication. This includes attention and listening, understanding language, expressive communication (spoken language and symbolic communication) and social communication skills. Therapists are based on site, allowing therapy to be fully integrated into daily school life and ensuring pupils receive consistent, joined-up support.
The SaLT team works closely with teaching staff and other therapy professionals to embed communication targets across all areas of learning throughout the school day. Each pupil is allocated a named speech and language therapist who delivers support in line with the provision set out in the pupil’s Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). Support may include direct therapy sessions, delivered on an individual, paired, small-group or whole-class basis, as well as indirect support through guidance to staff to promote communication-friendly practice across the school.
In addition, the SaLT team provides training and advice to school staff and families, helping to ensure consistency between home and school. Many pupils at SVIS use Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) to support their communication, and we adopt a total communication approach. Our therapists have experience working with a wide range of AAC systems, including signing, visual supports, core vocabulary boards, communication books, PECS, objects of reference and technology-based solutions such as switches, eye-gaze systems and voice-output devices. Where appropriate, we work collaboratively with specialist external services to support the effective use of AAC.
Our aim is to enable pupils to access learning as independently as possible, communicate confidently with others, develop meaningful relationships and build the skills needed to participate fully in school, at home and within the wider community.

pageCache.pageTitle: SENARP Vibe Independent School - Therapy Provisions
pageCache.text:
Therapy Provisions
At SENARP Vibe Independent School (SVIS), all pupils require carefully planned and highly individualised support as part of their daily learning experience. School staff play a vital role in supporting pupils throughout the day and receive ongoing training and guidance from therapy teams to ensure that pupils’ needs are met consistently and effectively.
By embedding universal therapeutic strategies across classrooms and the wider school environment, staff are equipped to support pupils proactively. This approach allows therapists to focus more intensively on pupils with complex needs and specific challenges, ensuring that support is both ef
Educational Occupational Therapy at SVIS is delivered using an evidence-based three-tier model, recommended for specialist education settings. This model ensures that therapy is integrated holistically across the school and recognises that pupils benefit from a combination of universal, targeted and specialist support rather than solely individual therapy sessions.
This layered approach ensures that every pupil receives appropriate support across the school day, while maintaining a strong focus on inclusion, independence and meaningful participation in learning.
